exposure: Exposure to nuclear waste or poisonous substances
cohort: The participants were 20 mothers of newborns with Oesophageal atresia and 30 control mothers whose children did not have OA.
finding: Maternal factors such as lower BMI prior to pregnancy, more pre-existing illnesses, allergies, higher rates of abnormalities during pregnancy, a history of previous abortions, German ethnic background, and increased daily dairy consumption were associated with the occurrence of Oesophageal atresia in offspring, alongside lower paternal socioeconomic status.
